content.title: 2026 UFL Rosters: Complete 50-Man Lineups for All 8 Teams, Including Every Former NFL Player
content.text: The UFL’s third season kicks off Friday with the most star-studded rosters in spring football history. Mike Repole’s controversial decision to liquidate all eight rosters and hold a league-wide draft has scattered familiar names across unfamiliar uniforms, but it has also concentrated NFL-caliber talent in ways the league hasn’t seen before. Complete 2026 UFL Team Rosters All eight teams finalized their 50-man rosters on March 23 following training camp in Arlington. The defending champion DC Defenders retained 12 players from last year’s title team, while the three expansion franchises in Columbus, Louisville, and Orlando built from scratch using players from the defunct Michigan Panthers, Memphis Showboats, and San Antonio Brahmas. WR, Birmingham Stallions (Jaguars, 2017-18) Deon Jackson, RB, DC Defenders (Colts, 2021-23) Jalen McKenzie, OT, Houston Gamblers (Titans, 2022) How the UFL to NFL Pipeline Remains Open in 2026 The UFL continues to serve as the NFL’s most active developmental league. Over the past two seasons, 66 players with connections to modern spring football have earned NFL roster spots or practice squad assignments. Multiple former spring kickers landed NFL jobs, including Brandon Aubrey and Jake Bates. For the players listed above, spring football offers the same proposition it always has: a platform, a paycheck, and a path back.
